lecture_context.lecture_title: Lecture 3: Full Cycle of a Deep Learning Project

unit.name: Sandboxing, error analysis, and data-centric improvement
unit.description: Connects empirical development to LLM prompting, responsible AI testing, error analysis, and targeted data improvement.
unit.summary: LLM applications follow the same empirical pattern because prompt behavior cannot be predicted fully from training data that no developer has inspected exhaustively [ts=1459s]. For responsible AI, the instructor recommends building and probing systems in sandbox environments before exposing users or third parties to possible harmful behavior [ts=1511s]. Error analysis connects model failures to next actions: teams can change architecture, change data, or add focused data for subsets where the system fails, such as face images with hats [ts=1667s]. Data-centric AI is defined as systematically engineering data to build a successful AI system, and the lecture warns against blindly collecting more data without identifying which subcategories matter [ts=1728s].

key_points.text: Prompting LLMs is empirical because model behavior cannot be predicted fully from enormous unseen training data.
Responsible AI testing should occur in a sandbox before the system affects innocent users or third parties.
Error analysis means examining where the model fails and using those failures to decide the next improvement.
Data-centric AI systematically engineers the data, not only the model, to improve the AI system.
More data is useful only when targeted to valuable subcategories rather than collected indiscriminately.

kp_catalog.name: Responsible AI sandbox testing
kp_catalog.description: AI systems, including LLM applications, should be built and probed in safe sandbox environments before being exposed to real users.
kp_catalog.importance_rationale: The concept is an important deployment discipline but occupies a shorter bridge section connecting empirical iteration to safety [ts=1511s].

kp_catalog.name: Error analysis
kp_catalog.description: Error analysis identifies where a model performs poorly and uses those failure patterns to choose the next model or data intervention.
kp_catalog.importance_rationale: Error analysis is the mechanism connecting model results to targeted data or architecture changes, and the instructor notes it will recur later in the course [ts=1646s].

kp_catalog.name: Data-centric AI
kp_catalog.description: Data-centric AI systematically improves or engineers the dataset to improve system performance, especially for observed failure modes.
kp_catalog.importance_rationale: The lecture explicitly names data-centric AI and uses hats, hair, glasses, and coding-data examples to show targeted data improvement [ts=1728s] [ts=1781s].
